Compile a Program

Source: R/client.R
pjrt_compile.Rd

Compile a PJRTProgram program into a PJRTExecutable.

Usage

pjrt_compile(
  program,
  compile_options = new_compile_options(),
  device = NULL,
  xla_options = list()
)

Arguments

program

(character(1))
A program to compile.

compile_options

(PJRTCompileOptions)
Compile options.

device

(NULL | PJRTDevice | character(1))
A PJRTDevice object or the name of the platform to use ("cpu", "cuda", ...), in which case the first device for that platform is used. The default is to use the CPU platform, but this can be configured via the PJRT_PLATFORM environment variable.

xla_options

(named list())
XLA compiler options for this compilation only. Each is named after a field of XLA's DebugOptions message (xla.proto), the names XLA_FLAGS takes without the leading --, and XLA applies it on top of its defaults and of XLA_FLAGS. The type of a value decides how XLA reads it: a logical(1) sets a boolean option, an integer(1) an integer option (or an enum by number), a double(1) a floating-point option, and a character(1) is parsed by the option's type – "True" or "False", a number, the name of an enum value, or a comma-separated list for a repeated option, which replaces its whole value. So an integer option takes 3L or "3", but not 3, and a single-precision option takes a double(1) only if it is positive, so 0 or a negative value has to be given as a string, e.g. "0". XLA reports an unknown name or a value of the wrong type when compiling.

An option of map type, such as xla_backend_extra_options, takes a character(1) in XLA_FLAGS syntax: comma-separated entries key=value, or key for an empty value, e.g. "xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion". Its entries are added to those the plugin applies by default, so entries set through XLA_FLAGS are kept. XLA does not check the entries: it ignores a key it does not know, and some keys count by their presence alone, so "xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion=false" turns that option on as well. On the CPU, XLA hands a key that does not start with xla_ to LLVM, which ends the R process if it does not know the key.

XLA's overrides cannot set a map, so pjrt reads the plugin's DebugOptions, with XLA_FLAGS applied, back from a small program it compiles once per client, adds the entries and sends the whole set. That differs from a compilation without map options in a few ways: XLA reads some options only when a compilation sends such a set (with xla_dump_to, it then also writes the compilation's inputs, and it dumps the small program too), and with --xla_flags_reset=true a later change to XLA_FLAGS does not reach compilations with map options. Reading the set back needs a plugin that reports the compile options it applies, which the CPU plugin does and the CUDA plugin does not; there, set the option through XLA_FLAGS before the plugin is loaded.

Value

PJRTExecutable

Examples

# Create a simple program
src <- r"(
func.func @main(\%arg0: tensor<2xf32>) -> tensor<2xf32> {
  return \%arg0 : tensor<2xf32>
}
)"
prog <- pjrt_program(src = src)
exec <- pjrt_compile(prog)
#> Error: -:2:17: error: unexpected character
#> <unknown>:0: error: Failed to parse using StableHLO v1.23.0, this could indicate forward incompatibility, >12w old unsupported plugin, or a portable artifact that needs to be further downgraded.

# Write the optimized HLO of this compilation to a directory
dir <- tempfile()
exec <- pjrt_compile(prog, xla_options = list(xla_dump_to = dir))
#> Error: -:2:17: error: unexpected character
#> <unknown>:0: error: Failed to parse using StableHLO v1.23.0, this could indicate forward incompatibility, >12w old unsupported plugin, or a portable artifact that needs to be further downgraded.
list.files(dir)
#> character(0)

# Keep XLA:CPU from duplicating cheap operations into the fusions that use them
exec <- pjrt_compile(
  prog,
  device = "cpu",
  xla_options = list(xla_backend_extra_options = "xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion")
)
#> Error: -:2:17: error: unexpected character
#> <unknown>:0: error: Failed to parse using StableHLO v1.23.0, this could indicate forward incompatibility, >12w old unsupported plugin, or a portable artifact that needs to be further downgraded.
